My associates and I determined to escape as soon as the craft drew close enough for us to be heard or spotted, as the moon, reaching fullness in two or three days, cast a brilliant light. Upon reaching the vessel, even if we proved unable to stop the strike looming over it, we could—and would—take every action the situation permitted. I suspected on multiple occasions that the Meridian was readying an assault; yet Captain Sorel merely permitted his opponent to draw near, only to retreat from it again.

Some of the night went by uneventfully. We kept a lookout for a chance to act. Because we were so deeply affected, we said very little. Tom Harlan wanted to leap into the ocean, yet I compelled him to hold back. In my estimation, the Meridian was going to strike the vessel at the waterline, which would make escaping not just feasible, but simple.

At three o’clock, gripped by anxiety, I climbed onto the platform. Captain Sorel remained there, stationed at the front by his flag, which a gentle wind unfurled over him. He kept his gaze fixed upon the ship. The power of his stare appeared to pull, captivate, and lure it forward with greater certainty than a towline could have. The moon was crossing the meridian at that moment. In the east, Jupiter ascended. Within this serene natural setting, the sky and the ocean vied in their stillness, the water providing the celestial bodies with the most exquisite mirror imaginable for their reflection. I trembled as I contrasted the profound quietude of the surroundings with the hidden emotions simmering inside the Meridian.

We were less than two miles away from the ship. It continued to approach the glowing luminescence that marked where the Meridian lay. I observed its red and green lamps, along with the white light suspended from the main foremast. A faint tremor ran across the rigging, indicating that the boilers were stoked to their maximum capacity. Streams of embers and crimson cinders erupted from the smokestacks, gleaming against the air like celestial bodies.

I stayed in that position until six o'clock, undetected by Captain Sorel. Positioned roughly a mile and a half away, the vessel commenced its bombardment again as the morning light broke. The time was nearing when the Meridian would strike its foe, allowing my associates and me to depart from this individual for good. I was getting ready to descend and alert them when the second officer arrived on the platform, followed by a group of sailors. Captain Sorel appeared either unable or unwilling to observe their presence. A few movements were made that served as the call to engage. These were quite uncomplicated. The metal railing encircling the platform was dropped, and the pilot cages and lantern were slid into the hull until they were level with the deck. The elongated exterior of the steel cigar now lacked any obstruction to its movements. I went back to the saloon. The Meridian was still afloat; a few rays of light were passing through the watery layers. As the waves swelled, the windows caught the crimson glow of the sun as it climbed, marking the arrival of this horrific 2nd of June.

The log indicated at five o’clock that the Meridian was losing velocity, and I understood that this permitted them to approach closer. Furthermore, the sounds of the reports grew clearer, and the shells, struggling as they moved through the surrounding water, were quenched with an odd hissing sound.
“The time has arrived,” I stated, “my friends. May God watch over us, and let us shake hands one last time!”

Tom Harlan remained firm, Baptiste stayed composed, and I was so anxious that I struggled to control my agitation. We entered the library together; however, the instant I nudged the door leading toward the main staircase, I caught the sound of the top panel snapping shut. The Canadian dashed toward the steps, yet I held him back. A familiar sibilant sound signaled to me that water was filling the tanks, and within moments the Meridian had descended several yards below the crests of the waves. I grasped the intent of the movement. Taking action was no longer an option. The Meridian did not intend to attack the solid armor, but rather the area under the waterline, where the metal plating provided no defense.

Once more we were held captive, forced to observe the horrific spectacle that was being readied. We barely possessed a moment to contemplate; retreating into my quarters, we stared at one another in silence. A profound numbness gripped my consciousness: my capacity for thought appeared frozen. I existed in that agonizing condition of anticipation that comes before a terrifying blast. I stood waiting, I remained attentive, my entire being concentrated solely upon the act of listening! The velocity of the Meridian increased. It was bracing to surge forward. The entire vessel vibrated. All at once I cried out. I sensed the impact, though it was relatively mild. I perceived the piercing force of the steel spur. I detected sounds of clattering and grinding. Yet the Meridian, driven by its own motive force, traversed the bulk of the ship as a needle moves through sailcloth!

My endurance had reached its limit. Driven to distraction, I bolted from my quarters and entered the saloon. Captain Sorel stood there, silent, sullen, and unyielding, gazing out the porthole. A massive object threw a dark shape across the sea; and, so that its suffering would remain complete, the Meridian descended into the depths along with it. A mere ten yards away, I spotted the breached hull, where water poured in with a thunderous roar, followed by the twin rows of cannons and the netting. The bridge teemed with dark, restless figures.

The tide climbed higher. Those wretched beings swarmed the ratlines, grasping at the masts, battling the waves. It resembled a colony of humans submerged by the ocean. Frozen, rigid from terror, my scalp prickling, eyes agape, gasping, winded, and mute, I also observed! A magnetic pull held me fast to the pane! Abruptly, a blast occurred. The trapped air shattered her decks, much like the ignition of the powder rooms. Subsequently, the doomed ship descended with greater speed. Her topmast, burdened with souls, emerged; followed by her spars, bowing beneath the mass of men; and, finally, the summit of her mainmast. Then the shadowy bulk vanished, along with the deceased company, pulled beneath by the powerful vortex.
The ill-fated ship descended with greater speed.

I faced Captain Sorel. That fearsome seeker of retribution, a flawless seraph of animosity, continued to gaze. Once everything had concluded, he pivoted toward his quarters, unlocked the entrance, and stepped inside. I tracked him with my vision. Upon the rear partition under his champions, I noticed the likeness of a female, yet youthful, and a pair of small offspring. Captain Sorel stared at them for a brief interval, reached his limbs in their direction, and, dropping to his knees, broke into profound weeping.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: The shutters had shut upon that ghastly sight, yet illumination failed to come back to the lounge: total quiet and gloom reigned inside the Meridian. With astonishing velocity, a hundred feet under the waves, it was departing that bleak location. Where was it headed? Toward the north or the south? Where was the individual fleeing to following such terrible retribution? I had gone back to my quarters, where Tom and Baptiste had stayed sufficiently quiet. I experienced an overwhelming revulsion for Captain Sorel. Regardless of what he had endured at the hands of those individuals, he possessed no justification to retaliate in such a manner. He had rendered me, if not a participant, at the very least a spectator to his retribution. At eleven the electrical illumination returned. I entered the lounge. It was empty. I examined the various gauges. The Meridian was racing northward at a pace of twenty-five miles per hour, at times on the water's surface, and at times thirty feet beneath it. Upon checking the coordinates on the map, I observed that we were traversing the opening of the Manche, and that our trajectory was rushing us toward the arctic waters at a terrifying velocity. During that night we had traversed two hundred leagues of the Atlantic. The darkness descended, and the ocean was shrouded in gloom until the moon appeared. I retreated to my quarters, but sleep eluded me. I was plagued by terrifying dreams. The ghastly spectacle of ruin was perpetually in my mind. From that point on, who could determine into which section of the North Atlantic basin the Meridian would carry us? Still with inexplicable velocity. Still surrounded by these arctic mists. Would it stop at Spitzbergen, or upon the coastlines of Nova Zembla? Might we investigate those mysterious waters, the White Sea, the Sea of Kara, the Gulf of Obi, the Archipelago of Liarrov, and the uncharted shore of Asia? I could not determine. I could no longer track the duration of time. The timepieces had been halted aboard. It appeared, as in arctic lands, that darkness and light no longer adhered to their typical cycle. I felt myself pulled into that bizarre territory where the collapsed fantasy of Edgar Poe wandered without restraint. Like the legendary Gordon Pym, at any instant I anticipated witnessing “that veiled human figure, of larger proportions than those of any inhabitant of the earth, thrown across the cataract which defends the approach to the pole.” I calculated (though, perhaps, I might be in error)—I calculated this daring journey of the Meridian to have continued for fifteen or twenty days. And I cannot say how much further it might have continued, had it not been for the disaster that concluded this expedition. Of Captain Sorel I observed nothing at all now, nor of his lieutenant. Not a single member of the ship's company was seen for a moment. The Meridian was nearly constantly submerged. When we ascended to the surface to replenish the oxygen, the shutters operated and closed automatically. There were no further indications on the globe. I was unaware of our location. And the Canadian, too, his vigor and endurance exhausted, was seen no more. Baptiste could not extract a syllable from him; and, dreading that, in a violent bout of insanity, he might take his own life, observed him with unceasing care. One morning (what day it was I could not say) I had drifted into a deep slumber near the dawn, a slumber both distressing and sickly, when I abruptly roused. Tom Harlan was hovering above me, stating, in a hushed tone, “We are going to fly.” I rose.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “At what time are we leaving?” I inquired.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “This evening. Every examination aboard the Meridian appears to have halted. Everyone seems dazed. Are you prepared, sir?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “Indeed; at what location are we?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “Land is visible. I calculated our position through the mist earlier today—twenty miles to the east.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “Which nation is this?”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “I am uncertain; however, regardless of its nature, we shall seek shelter within it.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “Indeed, Tom, indeed. We are going to take flight this evening, regardless of whether the ocean consumes us.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “The ocean is rough, the gale fierce, yet a twenty-mile journey in that small Meridian craft does not daunt me. Without the sailors’ knowledge, I managed to secure provisions and a few containers of water,” said I.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “I shall accompany you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “However,” the Canadian went on, “should I be taken unawares, I shall protect myself; I will compel them to slay me.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “Friend Tom, we shall perish as one.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: My decision was finalized. The Canadian departed from my side. I arrived at the deck, where the crashing of the swells made it hard to keep my footing. The heavens looked ominous; however, since those dense, dark silhouettes indicated land, our escape was necessary. I went back to the cabin, feeling both dread and anticipation at the prospect of encountering Captain Sorel, desiring and simultaneously dreading the sight of him. What words could I have offered him? Was it possible to mask the instinctive revulsion I felt in his presence? Impossible. It was preferable to avoid a direct confrontation; it was better to put him out of my mind. And yet—— That day felt interminable, the final one I would spend aboard the Meridian. I stayed by myself. Tom Harlan and Baptiste kept their distance, terrified of revealing their intentions. At six o'clock I ate dinner, though I lacked any appetite; I compelled myself to consume the meal despite my revulsion, so that my strength would not fail. At six-thirty Tom Harlan entered my quarters, stating, “We shall not see each other again before our departure. At ten the moon will not be risen. We will profit by the darkness. Come to the boat; Baptiste and I will wait for you.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: Without allowing me a moment to respond, the Canadian departed. I made my way to the saloon, intent on confirming the Meridian’s heading. We were traveling at a terrifying velocity in a north-northeasterly direction, submerged at a depth exceeding fifty yards. I took one final glance at these natural marvels, at the artistic wealth piled high within this gallery, and at the peerless assortment fated to be destroyed in the ocean depths alongside the man who had assembled it. I wanted to etch an unshakeable memory of the scene into my thoughts. For an hour, I stayed there, immersed in the glow of that radiant overhead light, examining the riches that glittered beneath their display cases. Afterward, I went back to my cabin.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: I donned sturdy nautical attire. Gathering my papers, I stowed them securely upon my person. My heart thundered. I found it impossible to restrain its rhythm. Without a doubt, my distress and restlessness would have revealed my state to the gaze of Captain Sorel. What was he occupied with at present? I stood listening by his chamber door. Footfalls reached my ears. Captain Sorel was inside. He had refrained from sleeping. I anticipated his emergence at any second, questioning my desire to flee. I remained perpetually vigilant. My mind amplified every detail. The feeling eventually grew so intense that I questioned whether it might be preferable to approach the room of the Captain, confront him directly, and defy him with my expression and movements.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: A lunatic’s notion had taken hold; luckily, I fought the urge, lying down upon my cot to soothe my physical tremors. My constitution settled slightly, yet within my fevered mind, I relived my entire duration aboard the Meridian; each occurrence, whether joyous or tragic, that transpired following my departure from the Evangeline—the underwater pursuit, the Torres Straits, the Papua natives, the grounding, the coral graveyard, the Suez transit, the Island of Santorin, the Cretan diver, Vigo Bay, Atlantis, the glacier, the South Pole, the entrapment within the ice, the battle against the squids, the tempest in the Gulf Stream, the Avenger, and the ghastly spectacle of the ship foundering with her entire company. These happenings paraded before my vision like acts in a play. Afterward, Captain Sorel appeared to expand vastly, his visage taking on godlike dimensions. He ceased to be my peer, becoming instead a creature of the deep, the spirit of the ocean.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: The time was nine-thirty. My head was gripped in my hands to prevent it from splitting apart. Shutting my eyes, I refused to continue thinking. Thirty minutes remained to be endured, another half-hour of this nightmare that threatened to shatter my sanity.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: Just then, the far-off notes of the organ reached me, a mournful melody accompanying a vague incantation, the cry of a spirit yearning to shatter its worldly chains. I remained motionless, barely inhaling, fully immersed; just as Captain Sorel was, in that melodic rapture that was pulling his soul toward the conclusion of existence.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: An abrupt notion then filled me with dread. Captain Sorel had vacated his quarters. He was positioned in the saloon, a space I was required to traverse in order to escape. It was there that I would encounter him one final time. He might notice me, or possibly address me. A movement from him could ruin me, and one utterance might bind me to the vessel.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: However, ten was nearing. The time had arrived for me to depart from my chamber and meet up with my associates.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: I cannot falter, not even should Captain Sorel appear in my path. I eased my door open; yet, as the hinges shifted, the sound struck me as terrifyingly loud. It is possible that the noise was merely a product of my mind.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: Moving stealthily up the Meridian’s unlit staircase, I paused on every tread to monitor my pulse. Upon arriving at the saloon entrance, I eased the door open. The interior was swallowed by deep shadow. A soft melody drifted from the organ. Captain Sorel occupied the room. He remained unaware of my presence. Even had the space been brightly illuminated, I doubt he would have perceived me, given how completely he was lost in his rapture.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: Moving across the rug, I took care to prevent even the faintest noise that could reveal I was there. It took me no less than five minutes to arrive at the entrance on the far side, which led into the library.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: Just as I prepared to unseal it, a sharp exhale from Captain Sorel froze me where I stood. I was aware that he was standing up. I could perceive his form, as the illumination from the library spilled into the saloon. He approached me without a sound, his arms folded over his chest, moving with the fluid grace of a phantom instead of a man. His lungs heaved with stifled weeping; and I caught him whispering these phrases (the final ones to reach my hearing):

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “Great God! stop! stop!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: Did a declaration of regret break free from the conscience of this man in such a way?

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: Driven by frantic need, I hurried across the library, ascended the middle stairs, and, after climbing the higher set, arrived at the boat. I slipped inside the gap, which had previously allowed my two companions to enter.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “We must depart! we must depart!” I cried.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “Immediately!” the Canadian answered.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: The aperture within the Meridian’s plating was initially sealed and secured using a spare key that Tom Harlan had brought along; the boat’s hatchway was likewise shut. The Canadian started to unscrew the bolts that continued to attach us to the submersible vessel.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: All at once, a sound rang out. People were calling back and forth in boisterous tones. Why was this happening? Was it possible that our escape had been found out? I sensed Tom Harlan sliding a blade into my palm.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “Indeed,” I whispered, “we understand the way to perish!”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: The Canadian had ceased his labor. Yet a single term, voiced again and again—a terrifying term—made clear the reason for the unrest rippling across the Meridian. It was not us that the sailors were seeking!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “The maelstrom! the maelstrom!” Could any term be more terrifying or any circumstance more dire to hear! We found ourselves positioned along the treacherous Norwegian shoreline. Was the Meridian currently being pulled toward that abyss just as our vessel prepared to depart? We understood that when the tide turns, the trapped currents between the islands of Ferroe and Loffoden surge with unstoppable force, creating a vortex that no ship can survive. Massive swells converged from every direction on the horizon, creating a chasm rightfully termed the “Navel of the Ocean,” which exerts a gravitational pull reaching out for twelve miles. Within that space, not merely ships, but also whales and polar bears from the north are claimed as victims.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: The Captain had steered the Meridian to that location, whether by choice or by force.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: A spiral was being traced, its perimeter shrinking incrementally, and the vessel, remaining tethered to its flank, was swept forward at a dizzying pace. I experienced that nauseating vertigo that stems from a prolonged rotation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: Terror gripped us. Our panic reached a peak, our blood flow ceased, every nervous impulse vanished, and we were drenched in a frigid perspiration, a sweat of pure torment! And the clamor surrounding our fragile vessel! The echoes of those bellows carried for miles! What a cacophony was created by the waves shattering against the jagged stones below, a place where the most resilient objects are pulverized and timber is eroded, “with all the fur rubbed off,” as the Norwegian expression goes!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: How precarious our position was! We swayed violently. The Meridian fought back as if it were a person. Its metallic sinews splintered. At times, the vessel appeared to rise vertically, and we were lifted along with it!

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: “It is necessary that we endure,” Tom remarked, “and attend to the bolts. Our rescue remains possible provided we remain with the Meridian.”

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: Before he could conclude his statement, a thunderous sound erupted, the fastenings snapped, and the vessel, ripped from its channel, was cast like a pebble from a catapult directly into the center of the vortex.

chapter_title: CHAPTER XXII THE LAST WORDS OF CAPTAIN SOREL
text: I hit my head against a fragment of iron, and the intense impact caused me to black out completely.

So concludes the journey beneath the ocean waves. I am unable to recount what transpired throughout that night, the manner in which the vessel eluded the whirlpool’s currents, or how Tom Harlan, Baptiste, and I managed to emerge from the abyss.

Upon regaining my senses, I found myself stretched out inside a fisherman’s hut situated on the Loffoden Isles. My two companions were close by, clutching my hands, unharmed. We hugged one another with great warmth.

We were unable to consider a trip back to France at that time. Connections linking the northern part of Norway to the south are infrequent. Consequently, I find myself compelled to await the monthly steamboat departing from Cape North.

In the company of those respectable individuals who have welcomed us so graciously, I am reviewing the chronicle of these experiences yet again. No event has been left out, and no particular has been overstated. This is an accurate account of our extraordinary journey through a realm beyond human reach, though one that Advancement shall eventually provide a path into.

Will my account be credited? I cannot say. Ultimately, it is of small consequence. My current assertion is that I possess the authority to discuss these waters, across which, in a period under ten months, I have traversed 20,000 leagues during that undersea voyage around the globe, an expedition that has unveiled such a multitude of marvels.

Yet what is the fate of the Meridian? Did it withstand the crushing force of the whirlpool? Is Captain Sorel alive? And does he continue to pursue those terrifying revenges beneath the sea? Or, did he cease following the final slaughter?

Might the ocean currents eventually deliver this record of his existence to him? Will I at some point discover the identity of this individual? Is the lost ship going to reveal the origin of Captain Sorel through its country of registration?

I trust it is. Furthermore, I pray that his mighty craft has mastered the ocean at its most fearsome abyss, and that the Meridian has endured in a place where countless other ships have perished! Should this be the case—if Captain Sorel continues to dwell within the sea, his chosen home, may malice be calmed in that fierce soul! May the sight of such marvels quench the urge for retribution for all time! May the magistrate vanish, and the thinker persist in the serene study of the deep! If his fate is peculiar, it is likewise magnificent. Have I not grasped it for myself? Have I not spent ten months in this abnormal existence? And to the inquiry posed by Ecclesiastes three millennia past, “That which is far off and exceeding deep, who can find it out?” only two men among all those currently alive possess the authority to provide a response——
CAPTAIN SOREL AND I.
